summary: Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) implemented every part of the proposal. A shared fetchWithDeadline (5 s primary, 10 s remote) bounds descriptor, session, ws-token and bootstrap fetches, including the body read. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken is retried and abortable. protocol.ts gives the URL provider the attempt signal and a 10 s timeoutOrElse that maps to the retried WsUrlProviderError. All direct/saved-env WsTransports on web and mobile set urlProviderTimeoutMs, except SSH, where the exclusion is deliberate. A saved-env slot timeout now aborts the attempt's controller and drops the pending entry, so a retry or Connect starts fresh. I found no unbounded control-plane fetch or URL provider left on the primary or direct saved-env paths. Two minor latent gaps remain: the mobile driver drops the supervisor's abort signal, and the web wrapper resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl does not declare `signal`. Each request in both cases is still deadline-bounded, so the described indefinite stall no longer happens.

evidence.note: Manual-timer deadline plus caller-signal merge. Promise.race on headers and body settles the caller even if the adapter ignores the signal, and controller.abort releases the socket. I read the edge cases (pre-aborted signal, unread body, repeated reads) and found no bug.

fetchControlPlane wraps every startup and reconnect call. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken(signal) goes through retryTransientBootstrap with signal-aware abandonment (118-138). The prefetched token uses the same 5 s-bounded requestWebSocketToken.
fetchRemoteJson uses the 10 s deadline. Session, rotate and ws-token URL resolution forward input.signal.

WS_URL_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS=10_000. tryPromise passes the attempt signal, and timeoutOrElse fails with WsUrlProviderError, which Effect.retry retries. Effect 4.0.2 timeoutOrElse→timeoutOption interrupts the loser, which aborts the signal.
WsTransport and DeviceWsTransport spread lifecycleHandlers (including urlProviderTimeoutMs) into createWsRpcProtocolLayer.
The primary /ws and /ws/device transports and the saved-env /ws and /ws/device transports all set urlProviderTimeoutMs. SSH is deliberately excluded. Hosted transports keep their own lifecycle.

There is one AbortController per pending attempt. The 60 s slot timeout calls abandonPendingSavedEnvironmentConnection, which deletes the entry, rejects joiners and aborts. supervision.test.ts:300-314 covers this.
The web saved-env connect forwards the attempt signal to the session check and to renewal rotate/session.

Minor latent defect. The wrapper resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl declares no `signal`. service.ts:1033 spreads `signal` in, which escapes excess-property checks, and it reaches fetchRemoteJson only because the wrapper forwards the whole input object. No test asserts the caller signal (api.test.ts checks only that a deadline signal is present).

Minor gap. The mobile driver's connectSavedEnvironment takes no signal, and the supervisor wiring (record, isCancelled) drops it, so a slot timeout on mobile does not abort the in-flight session check or renewal. The 10 s fetch deadline and the 15 s check timeout still bound both, and the pending entry is still dropped.

The SSH loopback fetch has no deadline and the SSH URL provider has no urlProviderTimeoutMs. ServerAliveInterval=15×CountMax=3 tears down a dead tunnel in about 45 s, so this is bounded rather than indefinite. The exclusion is intentional (service.ts:1100-1106).

I checked for a regression risk: client deadlines now abort a held bootstrap POST at 5 s. The gate drops held requests whose response closed and never replays them, so a one-time pairing credential is not consumed by an aborted request and the retry succeeds.

fixDefects: No blocking defects. Minor latent issues: (1) apps/web/src/environments/remote/api.ts:35-39 does not declare `signal` in the resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl wrapper type. Cancellation works only because the whole input object is forwarded, so a refactor that destructures it would silently stop aborting abandoned saved-env ws-token requests. (2) Mobile does not thread the supervisor's AbortSignal (environmentDriver.ts:380-383,446,619-620; environmentActions.ts:67-68), so a slot timeout on mobile leaves its session-check and renewal requests running to their 10-15 s deadlines instead of aborting them. (3) Out of scope and unchanged: primaryAuth post/get/getHubOrNull (primaryAuth.ts:256-293) have no deadline, but they are user-initiated pairing, Hub and E2EE operator calls. /ws/device-frames (service.ts:1005) resolves without a caller signal but is still bounded by the 5 s deadline and the 15 s retry window.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening only. (a) In apps/web/src/environments/remote/api.ts, add `readonly signal?: AbortSignal` to the resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl input type, and to issueRemoteWebSocketToken for symmetry. Add a case to apps/web/src/environments/remote/api.test.ts that passes an AbortController signal, aborts it mid-request, and asserts the call rejects with an AbortError-named cause. (b) In apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts, add a `signal?: AbortSignal` parameter to connectSavedEnvironment. Pass it to the remoteApi.fetchRemoteSessionState call at :446 and through renewalCalls(record, signal) for rotate/fetchSessionState during connect, but not for keepRenewed. Wire `(record, isCancelled, signal)` at :619-620, update the deps.connectSavedEnvironment type at :187-196, and change environmentActions.ts:67-68 to forward `(isCancelled, signal)`. Extend environmentDriver.test.ts so an aborted signal rejects the pending session check. Run focused vitest for apps/mobile/src/connection and apps/web/src/environments/remote only.
decisionReason: The leftover items are type and plumbing hardening with no auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol impact.
correction: No correction to the DONE status. The auditor's minor notes left out two small gaps: the mobile driver drops the supervisor abort signal (the auditor cited mobile only for the URL provider signal), and the web resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl wrapper type does not declare `signal`, so it is forwarded only incidentally.
